title: Noor and the Regiment
premise: In 1899, Wendell Yarrow, a mapmaker's apprentice raised in the silences of a workshop that serves both crown and smugglers, is left an orphaned child named Noor along with orders to erase every record of her existence. As Wendell completes the master's final atlas, they discover the maps themselves encode the regiment's crimes—massacres redrawn as rivers, villages folded into blank space. When Colonel Ashgrave comes to collect the atlas and the child, Wendell must choose between the safety of silence and the danger of truth. The workshop burns on the last night of the century; Wendell escapes with Noor and the one true map, trading belonging to the empire for a found family of two.
about_author: Lior Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial survey maps before turning to fiction. They write from a converted boathouse on the Oslofjord, where they keep a collection of deliberately inaccurate antique atlases.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Space
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On a frozen December morning, Wendell finds an infant abandoned at the workshop door with a note: forget this face. The master has been dead three months, his atlas unfinished, and Wendell alone knows which clients the maps truly serve. The beat is dread wrapped in tenderness—the first crack in twelve years of careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Master Drew Last
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cataloguing the master's papers to finish the atlas, Wendell discovers discrepancies: a valley that appears on no other survey, coordinates corrected in a shaking hand. Noor, now a fixture in the workshop, babbles at the maps as if she recognizes them. The emotional beat is dawning suspicion—the dead man may have been murdered for what he knew.

chapters.title: Visitors from the Capital
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Colonel Ashgrave arrives with two soldiers, courteous and cold, demanding delivery dates for the atlas and asking oddly specific questions about the master's final weeks. He notices Noor's cradle and says nothing—which frightens Wendell more than anger would. The beat is the suffocating performance of obedience while hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: The River That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with a flashback to the master's voice. Comparing the atlas against older surveys, Wendell decodes the pattern: places where the regiment operated have been erased or renamed. The master wasn't falsifying maps—he was preserving evidence inside them. The beat is horrified awe, followed by terror at understanding why the workshop still stands.

chapters.title: A Name for the Child
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A quiet interlude: naming Noor properly, teaching her letters with map legends, letting a found family form in the margins of danger. The neighbor Mrs. Okafor, who suspects everything, quietly leaves milk and coal without questions. The beat is warmth as stakes—the reader learns exactly what Wendell stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Second Set of Eyes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell realizes someone else has been reading the master's corrections: pages are subtly reordered, wax seals re-poured. A spy sits somewhere in the small circle of people who enter the workshop—and Noor's face matches a name in the erased valley. The beat is paranoia closing in; trust becomes a luxury.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Kindness
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The colonel returns alone, drops his officer's mask, and offers Wendell a bargain: finish the atlas faithfully, surrender the child, and be rewarded with a post in the capital. He reveals the master begged for the same mercy once. The beat is temptation articulated perfectly—the corruption of power offering itself as rescue.

chapters.title: Copying the Truth
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Working through freezing nights, Wendell secretly drafts a duplicate of the true map—the un-erased one—hiding it inside a child's sampler Noor embroiders. Mrs. Okafor reveals she was the master's informant and can move the copy to a printer in the capital. The beat is resolve hardening into action; silence finally broken by choice.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. New Year's Eve: Ashgrave returns with soldiers to collect the atlas and the girl. Wendell hands over the falsified atlas, and when Ashgrave discovers the substitution, he orders the workshop burned as an example. Wendell flees through the smoke with Noor as the old century dies behind them. The beat is the climax—everything lost but the truth carried out in a child's needlework.

chapters.title: Margins and Open Country
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, months later. In a coastal town, the true map reaches print under another name; the erased valley's survivors begin finding each other through its coordinates. Wendell teaches Noor to draw coastlines, honest ones. The beat is earned peace—not restoration but something better than belonging: a family built deliberately, mapping a world they intend to tell the truth about.
